readingMode: Direct full sequential text reading, reopening page-crossing clauses; original final page inspected visually.

coverage.authoredAnalysis: Cover is dated 26 June 2023 in Canarias and explicitly commits the signatories to Congress/Senate candidacies on 23 July 2023; proposes a common Canarian parliamentary group. This is a common manifesto, not every signatory party programme across Spain.
Campaign introduction on autonomy, rights, pandemic, war/climate and the election. Predictions/criticisms are attributed political arguments; no quiz consequences inferred.

Continuation of introduction and commitments 1-3: responsible governability, constitution/State of law, maximum self-government within a consensual plurinational State, and Canary Agenda agreement. Commitment 3 continues on page 4.

Commitments 3-9: protect Statute/REF, reject budgets breaching it, preserve investment parity and 75% resident transport discount, competition controls, statute/shore transfer development and freight-cost compensation. No causal claim about household prices is adopted as neutral fact.

Commitments 10-15: financing reform separate from REF; extend free buses/trams beyond 2023, fallback targeted groups, island railway finance; Canary exclusion from new international flight green levy; own representation in Morocco maritime/migration negotiations; ten-year extension of La Palma 60% income-tax discount; decent stable employment and training. Last measure continues on page 6.

Commitments 15-20: maintain Canary-specific employment programmes until employment reaches national level; permanent-job subsidies for youth 16-30, over-45s and underrepresented women; education pact; at least 42 million annual educational infrastructure funding; free first-cycle childcare (0-3) with sufficient public places, continued page 7.

Commitments 20-25: sufficient public childcare places, dual vocational training, study/travel scholarships when chosen education unavailable on home island; public pensions adjusted to living costs; poverty finance while above national rate; State 50% earmarked dependency-care funding, revised law continued page 8.

Commitments 25-29: flexible sustainable dependency-law review; constitutional fundamental health right, universal public healthcare and specific island/mental-health funding; protect gender-violence laws, apply Istanbul convention/state pact and oppose trafficking/exploitative prostitution; close gender gaps and special discrimination; shared care, childcare and improved parental leave. No specific duration inferred.

Commitments 29-34: equality across education/health/housing/sport/migration, LGTBI anti-discrimination and school harassment/health protocols; cultural and sports travel funding; preserve film-tax regional differential; diversified industry/tourism strategy and industrial overcost aid, continuing page 10.

Commitments 34-38: industrial regional incentive access; 100% national POSEI contribution and freight/farm insurance support; water-cost compensation and plant-health controls; at least 12% national bluefin-tuna quota and later no quota for named species. Party sustainability assertion is not independent ecological evidence. Science/innovation priorities continue page 11.

Commitments 38-40: astrophysics, marine science and biotech research priorities; digital-market access, correct VAT/IGIC mistakes and trading barriers; preserve resident transport discount, maximum reference fares specifically for public-service-obligation routes; not every international airfare.

Commitments 40-47: oversight of prices; capped public-service sea links among La Palma/El Hierro/La Gomera; State road agreement funding; special Canary airport regime; hydro-wind projects and energy-transition/climate time-series, island technology/oceanographic ship funding; international strategic cooperation continues page 13.

Commitments 47-52: West African peace/cooperation and adapted enterprise finance, Atlantic investment/research platform, EU coordinated sea rescue, irregular-migration cooperation plus solidarity across all autonomous communities for unaccompanied minors; State-financed/co-financed Canary police; broader childcare support and low-income targeting continued page 14.

End of commitment 52: national poverty threshold for free school meals, coverage from cited 13% to 29% childhood poverty, early educational support and more mental-health professionals. Signatory names in empty signature boxes visually inspected; do not claim handwritten signatures. No annex or footnotes beyond these 14 pages.
